seal.statement: The learner-side count check of a critical system partition refuses a spread-cure ADD's promotion in every failing nightly to 2026-09-19 (would_exceed_target_replica_count, maxAllowedVotersAfterPromotion 4): the priority-recovery overflow budget evaluated on the learner's node is 0 where the grants had 2. The refusal logs only the result, so which input zeroes the budget cannot be observed, and the static reproduction of 2026-09-18 could only offer a candidate. This quest makes the decision observable without changing it. Every count-check refusal, and the first count-check pass of each learner, logs the inputs the decision was actually made on, taken from the one evaluation that decided and never from a second read: the node readiness phase, reasons and the recovery-pending bit; whether a planning answer was present, its publication epoch and status, and its origin (fresh, memoized or retained) where its owner can state it; the priority summary's presence, satisfied flag, required distinct node count, ready eligible node count, blocked partition ids, this partition's ready distinct node count and spread gap, and which summary was chosen (derived or closure-refreshed); the planner entry for this partition (ready, spread gap, reasons); the active operation count with each counted operation's id, type, status and workflow step, the in-flight add-like replica ids and whether this learner owns one; the joining flag and the three promotion allowances; the completion state, reason code and temporary overflow voter budget; and the membership view - voter replica ids with their node ids, learner replica ids, the raw counts before the local-row correction, and the target replica count with its source. No decision, schedule, retry cadence, log message text or existing log field changes.

text: Made the learner-side count check's decided-on inputs observable without moving the decision. ONE evaluation now produces both the decision and the record of its inputs: observeLearnerPromotionCountCheck reads every source in main's order and exactly as often (measured on the unchanged tree: replica_operations 2, services 5, partitions 1, readiness snapshot 1, planning answer 1, node readiness 1 per check), returns a frozen observation, and evaluateLearnerPromotionCountCheck (new src/partition/learner-promotion-count-check.js, the arithmetic extracted verbatim) returns the outcome plus every intermediate state. The existing refusal line keeps its message and its four fields and gains one added field, countCheckInputs; the first count-check PASS of each learner emits one new info line, "Learner promotion count check inputs", carrying the same payload with the counts and cap nested (a consumer that discriminates deferrals by a top-level maxAllowedVotersAfterPromotion still sees only refusals). The payload names the readiness phase/reasons/recovery-pending bit, the planning answer's presence/epoch/status/origin, the priority summary's presence/satisfied/required and ready-eligible counts/blocked partition ids/source, this partition's planner entry (ready, spread gap, ready distinct node count, reasons), the active operation count with each counted operation's id/type/status/workflow step, the in-flight add-like replica ids and ownership, the joining flag and the three allowances, the completion state/reason code/temporary overflow voter budget, and the membership view with voter replica ids and node ids, learner replica ids, the raw counts before the local-row correction and the target with its source. Every list is capped at 8 and reports the entries it withheld. Two new owners state the provenance the guard cannot read off its answer, both BESIDE the object they describe so no diagnostic field can enter a memo key, identity, generation or equality: priority-partition-summary-source.js records which summary the derivation's final choice took (derived or closure_refreshed) in a WeakMap keyed by the chosen summary object, and priority-recovery-planning-answer-origin.js records the answer's origin (fresh, memoized or retained) in a WeakMap keyed by the planning owner; both read as an explicit unrecorded/unstated state when no owner stated one. Five witnesses: the refusal payload, the once-per-learner pass line, read counts plus poisoned second reads (the logged values are the first read's), the provenance naming (including a byte-identity assertion that the chosen summary gained no field), and a decisions-unchanged table of 8640 arithmetic rows plus 12 end-to-end guard rows compared against a frozen copy of main's arithmetic and overflow-budget rule kept in the test. Complexity baseline tightened 1819 -> 1818 on the checker's hint.

round 1 REJECT (2 blocking). B1: the change turns the test duplication ratchet red - npm run -s test:duplication exits 1 (794 clone groups / 30542 lines against the baseline 793 / 30519); the one new clone is test/partition/learner-promotion-count-check-inputs.test.js:849-872 <-> 815-838, the two ordinary-partition fixture blocks; the ratchet runs in the publish gate and in CI. B2: the planning answer's origin reports a retained answer as memoized on about 99 percent of reads on the real owner: resolvePriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswer memoizes whatever answer was produced, the retention layer's included, and on a hit records MEMOIZED over it (real ControlPlaneReadinessService instances in the formation simulator with only the retention decision forced: of 616 reads whose answer was the retained snapshot, 609 said memoized and 7 retained); the owner can state it - store the origin in the memo entry's value, never its key, and report the stored origin plus a served-from-memo flag; no witness covers the answer-memo path (a mutation recording FRESH on the answer-memo hit survives both witness files). Decision-neutral VERIFIED: an independent differential test loading main's real methods beside the staged ones, 3 seeds x 20,000 cases with two consecutive checks each (three partition classes, null and partial caches, every readiness getter of the fallback ladder, malformed rows and summaries, tables and answers changing between reads, faults at the k-th hit of each site), compared log level, message and every pre-existing field, schedule calls and reasons, proof-gate entry, thrown error text, role, leaderId, joining flag, timer and the ordered source-read trace: zero differences. one-evaluation: source reads identical in count and order; the pure controlPlaneReadinessService getter is read 3 times against main's 2 (the origin is read through a re-read of the getter, not the instance that answered) - harmless. diagnostics-never-decide holds: both registries are read only by the evidence path; on real owners origin read unstated 0 of 820 calls and source read derived wherever a summary existed. Hot path: payload built only on a refusal and the first pass; refusal path 10.3-11.0 us against main's 9.0-10.5. Payload about 2.5 KB, arrays capped at 8 with withheld counts. Log compatibility intact. Static otherwise green; the complexity baseline tightening 1819 -> 1818 is legitimate. Witness gaps (mutations that survive the witnesses but not the differential): the voter/learner census read order, the draining flag in recoveryPending, the payload built on every pass. Non-blocking: countActiveVoters, countPendingLearners and getTargetReplicaCountForPromotion are no longer called by the guard (dead production methods kept for tests); source 'derived' conflates the provided planning-snapshot summary with the locally derived one; capList freezes caller-owned arrays; the refusal line grows about tenfold at one line per second per refused learner; the attempt text overstates 'extracted verbatim' and 'frozen copy of main'.

Round-1 rejection repaired; both blocking findings are fixed and measured, and the three witness gaps the verifier named now kill their mutations.

B1 (test duplication ratchet red). The two ordinary-partition grid fixtures were literal copies of each other. ordinaryRow is hoisted to module scope and a shared ordinaryLeaderAndLearnerFixture builds the even-voter and joining-expansion rows, so the fixtures are declarations rather than duplicated row literals. npm run -s test:duplication is back at the baseline exactly: [test] 793/793 clone groups, 30519/30519 duplicated lines; [src+scripts] 57/57, 1845/1845. It is now part of the check sweep.

B2 (the origin lied about retained answers). The defect was a category error, not a missing call: the planning-answer memo caches whatever the retention layer produced, so recording MEMOIZED at the memo hit overwrote the fact that the answer was retained - 609 of 616 reads of a retained snapshot on real ControlPlaneReadinessService instances. The repair separates two independent facts. WHAT the answer is made of is marked on the answer OBJECT (a WeakSet in the origin owner) by markPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerRetained at the three retention returns, so the mark rides through every memo the answer passes. WHETHER this call rebuilt it is the projection memo's own fact, recorded per owner and node by recordPriorityRecoveryPlanningProjectionReuse. getPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerSync - the one place holding the FINAL answer - composes them at both of its returns via statePriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerOrigin. Nothing entered a memo key: readMemoizedPlanningAnswer still compares only generation and retainedAtEntry, and no field was added to any answer, summary or memo entry. The log reports origin (fresh, memoized or retained, with retained winning over memoized) and servedFromMemo separately, so a retained answer served from the memo reads retained and still says it was reused. On the verifier's own reproduction all 616 reads now read retained (609 servedFromMemo true, 7 false), against 609 mislabelled before. The answer-memo layer is now witnessed: a host with a non-null planning generation drives three reads through the real memo, proves the uncached resolver ran once, and asserts retained/retained/retained with servedFromMemo false/true/true. The line budget came back too: the oversized control-plane-readiness-priority-recovery-planning.js is +8 lines over main instead of +30, and the recorder lives in the origin module.

Witness gaps closed. The counting doubles now record an ORDERED read trace and can script a different services row set per read, so the guard's read order is pinned against main's own order (measured by running HEAD's copy of the guard over the same fixture): swapping the voter and learner censuses moves the voter count onto the second set and the witness dies. The draining flag is pinned by a pair - the same readiness reasons grant the promotion when not draining and refuse while draining - plus a grid row, so ignoring draining in recoveryPending dies in two witnesses. Payload construction is counted through a summary accessor only the evidence path reads (readyEligibleNodeCount): one build per refusal, exactly one across three passes, so building on every pass dies.

Non-blocking items fixed: the origin is read off the readiness-service instance the answer came from (captured once and passed into getPriorityRecoveryPlanningSnapshotForLearnerPromotion) instead of a second read of the property; capList always copies before freezing, so a caller's census array is never frozen underneath it; the summary-source owner now says in so many words that DERIVED names the derivation's base summary, which is itself already the more advanced of the snapshot's own summary and the local census.

Accuracy correction to the round-1 attempt text. The count-check arithmetic was MOVED into its own owner and RE-EXPRESSED, not transcribed verbatim: it is split into resolveReplacementPromotionAllowed, resolvePromotionAllowances, resolveAllLearnersFit and a single-return resolveCountCheckRefusal, where main had one inline boolean with a nested ternary for the reason. Its equivalence to main is proven rather than asserted - an exhaustive 8640-row grid against an independently written copy of main's expression form kept in the test (itself split in two for the complexity ratchet, so not textually identical to main either), plus the round-1 verifier's 60,000-case differential against main's real loaded methods, which found zero divergence in outcome, reason, cap, schedule calls, proof-gate entry, thrown text and the ordered read trace.

Also recorded for the owner: countActiveVoters, countPendingLearners and getTargetReplicaCountForPromotion now have no src caller at all - the guard reads the census and target owners directly. They are kept as one-line delegates because two tests pin them and one of those (test/bootstrap) is outside this quest's authorised trees; they cannot drift, since each delegates to the owner the guard uses.

Checks, all green on the staged tree: pre-commit hook exit 0; test:complexity 1818/1818; test:complexity:cognitive 160/160; test:duplication at baseline; audit:shards; test:unused:push; audit:file-size 27/27 and 21/21; audit:guidelines 0 new in every audit; the evidence harness 5/5 and the probe metric 0. Mutation matrix re-run at 21 mutations, every one anchored (a mutation whose anchor is missing now fails loudly rather than passing as a no-op - the round-1 matrix had one such silent no-op), every one red on its witness and green after restore.

round 2 REJECT (1 blocking). B1 fixed (test duplication back at 793/793 and 30519/30519). B2 as stated fixed (the two reproductions read retained on every read of the retained snapshot, 616 of 616, servedFromMemo true on 609; the retentionOwner witness is real). B3 (new): the WeakSet mark leaks onto an answer the retention layer did not produce. markPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerRetained marks the active-snapshot object itself, and that object is the node's current sync projection, stored by getPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerSync's early return and still served by the projection memo; a different consumer's retention return (MembershipPublicationCoordinatorQueue.readPublicationPlanningSnapshot -> getAllNodeReadiness -> evaluateNodeReadiness -> resolveNodeMembershipPublicationPlanningAnswer -> buildDirectMembershipPublicationPlanningAnswer -> resolvePriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswer, on a joiner whose direct-row snapshot has no epoch, where the real shouldRetainMoreRecentActive answers true) marks it, and every later guard read - an early return, where the retention layer is never consulted - is stated retained with servedFromMemo true until the projection memo rotates. Real owners in the formation simulator, seeds 7, 8 and 21, nothing forced: 2532 of 2532 guard-path calls took the early return, 45 retention returns came from other paths, 3 guard reads were stated retained; 9 of 9 such retention events marked exactly the object the node's projection memo was serving. Minimal reproduction with the real store, shouldRetain and memo: guard read 1 fresh, one resolvePriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswer on another path, guard read 2 of the same object stated retained where the truth is memoized; driven through the staged guard the refusal lines read fresh, memoized, retained, retained. It is B2's class with the opposite sign and would falsely confirm a stale-retained-answer diagnosis. Fix direction: retained is a fact of the call path, not of the object - the early return must state the origin without honouring the mark, or carry retained on the answer-memo entry value or a per-call flag composed at the final return; add the witness (guard read, a retention on another path over the same object, a guard read that must not say retained). Decision neutrality re-verified: the same differential, 3 seeds x 20,000 cases with two checks each against main's sha-checked methods, zero decision, error, state or ordered-trace differences; the readiness-service getter is read once against main's two. Real-owner provenance, passive, 2532 calls: origin fresh or memoized with 0 unstated, servedFromMemo right on every call against object-identity ground truth, source derived wherever a summary existed. The mark is never lost (the object is not copied or normalized between a retention return and the guard). Process risk checked: git diff empty, every src hunk of the round-to-round diff intentional, no reference to removed names, every export used, receipt digests match. Statics all green including duplication; complexity 1818/1818; the oversized planning file is +9 lines over main. Round-1 surviving mutations now die (read order, draining, payload built on every pass, the mark ignored when stating). Witness gaps (non-blocking): the second and third retention returns unmarked survive (the third, the merged projection, is the common product); servedFromMemo forced false in the payload survives because no witness drives the guard against a real planning owner; capList freezing the caller's array, the origin read through a second getter read, and the reuse record ignoring the node survive.

Round-2 rejection repaired: `retained` is now a fact of the CALL PATH, not of the answer object, and the leak is gone on real owners.

B3, the defect. markPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerRetained marked the answer OBJECT. The object the retention layer hands back is the node's active snapshot, which is also what the projection memo serves to everybody else, so a retention event raised on another consumer's path (readPublicationPlanningSnapshot -> getAllNodeReadiness -> evaluateNodeReadiness -> resolveNodeMembershipPublicationPlanningAnswer -> buildDirectMembershipPublicationPlanningAnswer -> resolvePriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswer, on a joiner whose direct-row snapshot has no epoch) tainted every later guard read of that object - reads that take the early return and never consult retention at all. It is B2's class with the opposite sign: it would falsely confirm a stale-retained-answer diagnosis.

The repair. The object mark is REMOVED entirely; no object-keyed state remains, so nothing can be inherited. The origin owner now keeps one per-owner call record, {nodeId, servedFromMemo, retained}, reset by beginPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswer at the top of getPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerSync - so nothing an earlier call or another consumer's path observed survives into this one. The three retention returns call notePriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerRetention(this, nodeId, answer), which sets the flag for THIS call and hands the answer straight back. Retention that must outlive its call rides on the answer-memo entry's VALUE: storeMemoizedPlanningAnswer reads the call flag through readPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerCallRetention and stores it beside the answer, and a memo hit re-notes it for the new call; readMemoizedPlanningAnswer still matches on the generation and the retained witness alone, so nothing entered a key. The early return cannot state retained by construction, because it never reaches a note. Every record is read only when its nodeId matches the node being asked about.

Measured. The verifier's own acceptance scripts, unmodified: r2-taint-minimal now reads fresh then memoized where it read fresh then retained; r2-taint-e2e-log reads fresh, memoized, memoized, memoized where it read fresh, memoized, retained, retained; r2-retained-masked still reads retained on all three reads of a genuinely retained answer, servedFromMemo false, true, true, so B2 stays fixed. On real ControlPlaneReadinessService instances in the formation simulator, seeds 7, 8 and 21, nothing forced: 2532 answer-sync calls, earlyReturnLabelledRetained 0 (was 3), servedFromMemoWrong 0, and the whole histogram is fresh or memoized with 0 unstated, while the 45 other-path retention returns no longer reach the guard's reads at all.

Witnesses added, all six the round-2 review asked for. W1 the leak itself: a guard read builds and takes the early return, another path's resolve is handed that very object and the assertion proves it is the same object, and the next guard read must read memoized. W2 each of the three retention returns separately, driven by a shape selector - the complete-and-retain branch, the incomplete branch with no resolution of its own, and the incomplete MERGED branch that is the common product live - each asserted to state retained. W3 the guard end to end against a REAL planning owner: createSimulatedNodeHosts over a virtual network gives a real ControlPlaneReadinessService with its real cache, CDC service, publication coordinator and planning memos, the real guard bag reads it, and the logged payload is asserted fresh with servedFromMemo false on the first check and memoized with servedFromMemo true once the real projection memo serves, with no read ever unstated or retained. W4 capList leaves a caller's array mutable, capped or not. W5 the readiness-service property is read exactly once per check and the origin comes off that same instance - the double hands out a fresh instance per read, so a second read would lose the origin. W6 a reuse record taken for another node never answers for this one.

Mutation matrix re-run at 29, every one anchored, every one red on its witness and green after restore, with the repair STAGED first so restores come from the index. Every mutation the round-2 verifier found surviving now dies: servedFromMemo forced false in the payload, each of the three retention returns unnoted, capList freezing the caller's array, the origin read through a second getter, and the reuse record ignoring the node. New ones added for this repair: the call facts never reset, the answer memo dropping its stored retention, and a memo hit outranking retention.

Line budget. The oversized control-plane-readiness-priority-recovery-planning.js is +15 lines over main (1052 to 1067) against +9 before; the added lines are the three note wraps, the memo-hit re-note, and the memo entry's retained field with its comment. The recorder stays in the origin module.

Checks, all green on the staged tree: pre-commit hook exit 0; test:complexity 1818/1818; test:complexity:cognitive 160/160; test:duplication at baseline in both lanes; audit:shards; test:unused:push; audit:file-size 27/27 and 21/21; audit:guidelines 0 new; the evidence harness 5/5 and the probe metric 0. 31 affected test files re-run, all passing.

round 3 APPROVE (0 blocking) on index tree 159972c6437c750751e45fa24a7b40ed0611f526 at 3e186639d. B3 fixed on real owners: 2532 guard calls, 0 early returns labelled retained, 0 wrong servedFromMemo, 0 unstated; forced retention 616/616 retained. Per-owner call record: max call depth 1 over 4172 answer-sync calls in three modes, 0 nested calls (the projection build defers nested planning), begin resets after a throw.
